claim: The QVenture rubric separates deals on disclosed evidence, including business models that have no SaaS metrics.

revisions: 2026-07-26 (first): 24 cases, capital-intensive arm had n=1 success — that split was not a measurement and was labelled as such.

2026-07-26 (this): corpus extended to 32 with 8 capital-intensive cases (SpaceX, Moderna, First Solar, Enphase, Illumina succeeded; Northvolt, Solyndra, Nikola failed), and the engine learned two adverse disclosures those cases surfaced — production/schedule shortfall and a capital requirement far beyond the round.

calibration.note: Reconstructed descriptions of companies with public outcomes, written with hindsight. Measures DISCRIMINATION and RANGE only — never predictive accuracy.
calibration.caveat: Fixtures state few figures, so rubric v5's non-SaaS evidence layer fires on only part of this corpus — the hard-cases harness is what measures that capability. Northvolt is the instructive case: the largest contracted backlog in the corpus, and it failed. It scored 60.5 (above the mean success) until the engine also read the two negatives its own disclosure stated; it now scores 55.7 with two flags.

hardCases.note: Matched strong/weak pairs inside one sector and stage, so sector priors are held constant and the gap comes only from what the plan discloses.

openIssues: On plans that disclose no figures at all, the composite still compresses into roughly 50-68 of a nominal 0-100 scale. That is defensible (no evidence, no movement) but the scale as presented overstates its own resolution.

No case in the calibration corpus reaches 'invest'. On disclosure-rich input the hard-cases harness does reach it (marketplace strong, 72.6), so the band is reachable — but not on evidence-free descriptions.
8 of 15 known failures still score at or above the weakest known success. This corpus cannot support any claim about predicting outcomes, only about spreading disclosed evidence apart.
